skill.name: ddd-check
skill.description: Checks Java projects against Domain-Driven Design rules for layering, dependencies, naming, base classes, identity protection, and common anti-patterns.
skill.summary: Review changed files or a complete Java project for actionable DDD compliance issues.
skill.author: bookiosk

content.user_title: Audit Java Projects for DDD Compliance
content.value_statement: DDD violations can hide across Java layers and weaken architecture boundaries. This skill reviews changed files or complete projects against documented, actionable rules.
actual_capabilities: Checks changed Java files through an incremental git diff workflow.
Audits all non-test Java files during a full architecture review.
Validates package placement and dependencies across six DDD layers.
Checks required base classes and protected identity setters.
Detects naming violations and documented DDD anti-patterns.
Reports severity, rule references, and specific remediation guidance.
limitations: Applies the bundled architecture conventions, which may differ from project standards.
Reviews Java source and does not compile, test, or execute the application.
Incremental mode requires a Git repository with a useful HEAD diff.
Full audits can be slow for large repositories because every Java file is reviewed.

use_cases.title: Pre-commit DDD Review
use_cases.description: Check changed Java files before committing and fix layer, naming, or dependency violations early.

use_cases.title: Pull Request Architecture Check
use_cases.description: Review a change set against shared DDD rules and produce specific findings for reviewers.

use_cases.title: Full Project Assessment
use_cases.description: Audit every production Java file to identify architecture drift and prioritize remediation.

prompt_templates.title: Check My Changes
prompt_templates.prompt: Run an incremental DDD check on my changed Java files. Report each violation with severity, rule reference, and a specific fix.

prompt_templates.title: Review One Layer
prompt_templates.prompt: Review changed files in the domain layer. Focus on aggregate boundaries, base classes, identity protection, repository interfaces, and forbidden infrastructure dependencies.

prompt_templates.title: Audit the Project
prompt_templates.prompt: Run a full DDD audit of this Java project. Summarize findings by layer, show dependency violations, and prioritize recommended fixes.

prompt_templates.title: Plan Architecture Remediation
prompt_templates.prompt: Perform a full DDD audit, group related violations by root cause, and propose a staged remediation plan with dependencies and expected impact.

output_examples.input: Check my changed Java files for DDD compliance.
output: Three Java files reviewed in the domain and application layers.
High: OrderAggregate exposes a public identity setter. Make the setter protected under the domain identity rule.
Medium: CreateOrderService uses an abstract service name. Rename it to express command intent.

output_examples.input: Run a full architecture audit and prioritize the findings.
output: The audit found one critical dependency violation and four convention issues.
Priority 1: Remove the infrastructure Mapper import from the domain layer.
Priority 2: Align repository and application service base classes with the bundled rules.

best_practices: Use incremental mode during daily development and full mode before releases.
Confirm that the bundled conventions match project decisions before enforcing findings.
Address dependency-direction and identity-protection findings before naming or style issues.
anti_patterns: Do not treat every finding as correct without checking project context.
Do not run a full audit when only a small change set needs review.
Do not suppress architecture violations only to reduce the finding count.

faq.question: Which projects can this skill review?
faq.answer: It reviews Java projects organized around the bundled Domain-Driven Design layer conventions.

faq.question: What is the difference between incremental and full mode?
faq.answer: Incremental mode checks changed Java files. Full mode reviews every production Java file in the project.

faq.question: Does the skill change source files?
faq.answer: No. It reads source files and reports suggested fixes without editing application code.

faq.question: Does the skill run tests or compile the project?
faq.answer: No. It performs a source-based architecture review and does not validate runtime behavior.

faq.question: Can teams customize the rules?
faq.answer: The audit follows the bundled rule files. Teams must update those documents to reflect different conventions.

faq.question: What does a critical finding mean?
faq.answer: It indicates a major architecture violation, such as a forbidden dependency from the domain layer to infrastructure.
